newsitem.title: USA: Train carrying gas, acid derails near San Francisco.
newsitem.headline: Train carrying gas, acid derails near San Francisco.

text.p: At least 19 cars of a train carrying gas residue and corrosive acid derailed late on Friday near Martinez, Calif., forcing the evacuation of some homes in the area, authorities said.
Fire and sheriff department officials at the scene said residents were being evacuated within a half-mile of the accident as a precaution.
PG&E Corp.'s Pacific Gas and Electric Co. said it was asked by local authorities to cut off gas and electric service to homes in the immediate area.
"They don't want any possible source of ignition," PG&E spokesman Lyle LaFaver said.
There were no immediate reports of injuries or leaks and the cause of the derailment was not immediately known.

The accident occurred at about 5:30 p.m. local time/8:30 p.m. EDT (0030 GMT Saturday) about 25 miles (40 km) northeast of San Francisco. The two-locomotive, 60-car Burlington Northern Santa Fe freight train was travelling to nearby Richmond, Calif., when it jumped the tracks.
Burlington Northern spokesman Michael Martin said the train's two-person crew was not hurt in the accident.

Martin said 47 of the 60 freight cars were loaded. Of the 19 cars that derailed, he said 10 contained liquefied petroleum gas residue, two contained phosphoric acid and one was full of paint. The other cars that derailed were carrying wheat, tin products and fiber.
Martin said both cars containing acid were upright. "They did not tumble down the hill," Martin said, adding that a Burlington Northern hazardous materials team was on the scene.
